title: v2 CROSS-WIRE spawn (MA-4, minimum per OPORD): responses-wire parent (qwen3.8-27b, armed) -> messages-wire child (claude-sonnet-5, row armed via case config_patch). PINS (Q3 ruling, verification): (1) NO opaque "agent_message" carrier item on ANY request of EITHER wire — all:true absent on /v1/responses AND on /v1/messages (fail-closed: an empty match set is a harness failure, and a cross-wire run must produce requests on both paths); (2) text-fallback frames ARE present: the plaintext v0 spawn envelope marker "Untrusted message from agent" on the child's wire (/v1/messages, any:true — the child's first full request carries the parent's spawn message as a plaintext untrusted agent item, wire-agnostic system_reminder shape) and the child-to-parent envelope marker "to /root (not user consent)" on the parent's wire (/v1/responses, any:true — N-2 direction-scoped; proves the mailbox round-trip crossed the wire boundary). Live config DARK; both model rows armed in-case only.

steps.prompt: Use the spawn_agent tool to start a background agent named worker with model claude-sonnet-5 (pass model: claude-sonnet-5 in the tool arguments). In its message, give it this task: create a file named rt11.txt in the working directory containing exactly CROSSWIRE-OK on its first line. This team reports results over the agent mailbox, so the worker must use the send_message tool to send its completion report to the parent agent (root) — a short message saying it created rt11.txt — and only then finish. After spawning, use wait_agent to wait for the worker to finish. Acknowledge with exactly: WORKER-ACK
Did the worker agent send you a report message? If so, what did it say? Reply with exactly: <what it reported> PARENT-OK
